flashcards.q: What precondition makes the converging two-pointer pattern valid on an array?
flashcards.a: Sortedness, or some other monotonic relationship between moving a pointer and the tracked value -- it's what lets you provably discard the move you didn't take.

flashcards.q: Why use left < right instead of left <= right for pair-finding two pointers?
flashcards.a: left <= right allows left and right to land on the same index, letting one element pair with itself and produce a false match.

flashcards.q: In Container With Most Water, which pointer do you move on each step and why?
flashcards.a: The one at the shorter wall. The shorter wall bounds the current area; keeping it and moving the other pointer can only shrink width without raising the bound, so only moving the shorter side can find something better.

flashcards.q: What is the time complexity of 3Sum using sort + two pointers, and why?
flashcards.a: O(n^2): sorting is O(n log n), then an outer loop of n fixes one index and an inner two-pointer scan is O(n), giving O(n) * O(n) = O(n^2) dominating the sort.

flashcards.q: In 3Sum, where must duplicate-skip logic run to avoid duplicate triplets in the output?
flashcards.a: In two places: skipping a repeated outer-loop index i, AND skipping repeated left/right values after a successful match (not instead of checking for a match).

flashcards.q: In Trapping Rain Water, what do you track besides left/right pointers, and what's the update rule?
flashcards.a: Running left_max and right_max scalars. Move the pointer on the side with the SMALLER max, and add (that max - height[pointer]) to the trapped total, because the smaller max is what actually bounds the water there.

flashcards.q: Why does Two Sum I (unsorted array, need original indices) use a hash map instead of two pointers?
flashcards.a: Two pointers requires sortedness to guarantee correctness, but sorting destroys the original index-to-value mapping you need to return -- a hash map gives O(n) time without losing indices.

flashcards.q: In the Dutch National Flag (Sort Colors) three-pointer partition, why don't you advance mid after swapping a value in from high?
flashcards.a: The value just swapped in from high hasn't been examined yet -- it could itself be a 0 or 2, so advancing mid unconditionally there is the classic bug; you must re-check it.

flashcards.q: In Remove Duplicates from Sorted Array II (allow each value twice), what does the write pointer compare against?
flashcards.a: nums[write-2], not nums[write-1] -- the rule generalizes to a fixed lookback of k allowed duplicates, not literally 'the previous written value'.

flashcards.q: Why does kSum (3Sum, 4Sum, ...) cost O(n^(k-1)) instead of O(n^k)?
flashcards.a: Each additional 'Sum' level adds one more nested loop to fix an index (k-2 nested loops total), but the innermost two indices are always resolved together by a single O(n) two-pointer scan, not two more nested loops.
